english: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}-1&1&0\\-2&2&1\\2&-1&2\end{pmatrix}$. Then the sum of all the entries of $A^{10}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $A=\begin{pmatrix}-1&1&0\\-2&2&1\\2&-1&2\end{pmatrix}$ है। तब $A^{10}$ की सभी प्रविष्टियों का योग ______ है।
solution: $N^{2}=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&1\\4&-2&2\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $N^{3}=N^{2}N=O$ (row $1$ of $N^{2}$ times $N$ is $(0,0,0)$, row $2$ is twice row $1$)
$I$ and $N$ commute, so by the binomial theorem $A^{10}=I+10N+\binom{10}{2}N^{2}=I+10N+45N^{2}$
solution_full: The sum of entries is linear: sum$(I)=3$, sum$(N)=-2+1+0-2+1+1+2-1+1=1$, sum$\left(N^{2}\right)=2-1+1+4-2+2=6$.
Hence the sum of the entries of $A^{10}$ is $3+10\cdot1+45\cdot6=3+10+270=283$.
originality_note: New: the nilpotent part is hidden in a non-triangular integer matrix (A - I has trace 0 and N^3 = O but no zero pattern), so the student must test A - I before expanding (way 4). Closest known: A = I + N with N strictly upper triangular (JEE Main 2021 type) and the NCERT nilpotent matrix [[1,1,3],[5,2,6],[-2,-1,-3]]. Different because: the matrix is new and not triangular, so the I + N split must be discovered.

concept_use.Higher powers using A = I + N with N nil: A - I = N has N^3 = O with N^2 != O, so A^10 = I + 10N + 45N^2 by the binomial theorem.
